paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
coupling_convention: |g^3_aN| isovector axion-nucleon coupling in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on y-axis (also applies to g_an as visual reference per caption)
notes: Paper derives a new 95% CL exclusion on the isovector axion-nucleon coupling from axion-induced deuteron dissociation (a + d -> n + p) using the full SNO solar neutrino dataset. The bound is mass-independent: |g^3_aN| > 2e-5 GeV^-1 excluded for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV (encoded as a flat two-point line; low-mass end taken from Fig. 1 axis at 1e-22 eV). The exclusion has an UPPER edge at ~1e-3 GeV^-1 due to solar trapping (axions with stronger couplings are trapped in the Sun), so the excluded band is 2e-5 to 1e-3 GeV^-1. Coupling type set to AxionNeutron per the generic-nucleon convention, but note the actual constrained quantity is the isovector combination (g_an - g_ap)/2; it maps onto g_an only assuming no fine-tuned cancellation between g_an and g_ap. Values emitted are raw GeV^-1 derivative couplings as quoted in the paper. No DM assumption (solar axion flux, not haloscope). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.65, 32)) | Vision: Main result is the blue SNO band: flat lower boundary at |g^3_aN| = 2e-5 GeV^-1 from 1e-22 eV up to ~1 MeV (plot edge), quoted valid to ~5.5 MeV; upper boundary at 1e-3 GeV^-1 from solar trapping. Coupling is the ISOVECTOR nucleon combination (g_ap - g_an)/2 style, dimensionful in GeV^-1, not the canonical dimensionless g_an — emitted values are exactly as plotted.
